notes: Lens: under-strictness and coverage holes. All 64 checks were fired against constructed envelopes through the pure engine; 63 fired at their catalogued severity, FINDINGS_TRUNCATED is unreachable (max constructible report = 86 findings vs a 200 cap). Baseline: worker/positive-control.js grades A with 60 checks run. Three false-negative families dominate. (1) TYPE COERCION — payTo/asset/maxTimeoutSeconds are tested through String()/Number() coercion, so ['0x…'], 'USDC', '60', ['60'] and true all grade A while @x402/core's zod rejects the type and @x402/evm's viem getAddress throws. (2) SEVERITY TOO GENTLE for hard client failures — an accepts entry with no `extra` grades B in BOTH generations, yet @x402/evm:555-560 throws before signing and the v1 signer produces a truncated EIP-712 domain; v1 mimeType, description and maxTimeoutSeconds are REQUIRED by x402@1.2.0's PaymentRequirementsSchema (a missing one is a ZodError on accepts[0]) and are graded warn; a v1 network outside the 17-name enum and a v1 scheme other than 'exact' grade A while x402-fetch throws. (3) LIMITS STATED BUT NOT ENFORCED — serviceName ≤32 printable ASCII and tags ≤5×32 are normative in bazaar.md:389-390 and enforced by ResourceInfoSchema, and the linter's own fix text names both, but neither is checked; resource.url is not required to be https despite CDP's required url_https preflight; amount has no floor despite CDP's required '>= 1000' check; the 500-character description limit the fix text asserts has no source anywhere in specs/. #3045 wire-format bug coverage: bug 1 (x402_version) CAUGHT by V2_VERSION; bug 3 (relative resource.url) CAUGHT for v2, MISSED for v1 (V1_RESOURCE_STRING is presence-only where the client is z.string().url()); bug 4 (bazaar input/output type discriminator) MISSED — V2_BAZAAR_INPUT is isObject-only and info.output.type is unchecked; bug 5 (external $ref) MISSED — json-schema.js:151-157 silently ignores an unresolvable $ref, which is bazaar.md:321's explicit MUST-NOT. TWO CLASSES THE CATALOGUE MISSES ENTIRELY. (a) #3045 bug 2, the request-header contract: the server must read PAYMENT-SIGNATURE for v2 and X-PAYMENT for v1 (transports-v2/http.md:57,169; x402-fetch/dist/esm/index.mjs:46). No check exists, and none can be written from a single unauthenticated response — it needs a second probe carrying a dummy PAYMENT-SIGNATURE header, which is a fetch-layer capability the engine does not have. Worth a catalogue entry plus a probe, because it was one of five confirmed production bugs. (b) paymentPayload.resource — #3045's one confirmed-real engineer lead ('required for the discovery job to be submitted, not part of the base x402 spec'). It is a settle-path field; the closest the catalogue gets is V2_RESOURCE_OBJECT, since @x402/core/client/index.js:413 copies the envelope's resource into the payload, so a v2 envelope with a proper top-level resource populates it for free. A v1-only or resource-less seller cannot. Worth naming in V2_RESOURCE_OBJECT's fix text as the discovery consequence. Non-holes checked and cleared: viem 2.55.18 getAddress does NOT enforce EIP-55, so a bad-checksum mixed-case address is correctly tolerated; padding-stripped base64 is legal under Base64EncodedRegex; DUAL_PAYTO/DUAL_ASSET correctly lowercase both sides; V2/V1_AMOUNT_ATOMIC's /^\d+$/ is strictly tighter than either client's own amount validation.
